jointHelp: This path considers these conditions together. One alone is not enough. Their positions inside the frame do not specify the order of events.
alternativeHelp: These branches represent different mechanisms. They do not all have to occur, though more than one can occur together.
watch: What new evidence would change this assessment?
additionalConditions: What would need to come together?
limitations: How far does the evidence go?
reportIssue: Report an error or unclear explanation
permalink: The URL links directly to this item
overdueNote: Recent changes may not be reflected yet. Passing a review date does not, by itself, mean the content is wrong.
newsIntro: Let’s place a report on the map and separate what it tells us from what remains uncertain.
freshnessTitle: A few months can change the picture.
freshnessIntro: As a rule, we revisit capability and behavior claims every 7 days, pathway assumptions every 30 days, and primarily definitional entries every 90 days. Important new evidence prompts an earlier review.
freshnessMeaning: “Review due” is a reminder to check for recent changes. It does not measure error or danger.
reviewCount: {count} items have reached their review date
updateStep1Text: Track capability gains, incidents, improved safeguards, replications, and counterevidence.
updateStep2Text: Separate publication and study dates, then identify which claims and connections change.
updateStep3Text: Review proposed changes and their reasons, then record accepted revisions.
about1: This map asks what might follow if certain conditions come together. It does not forecast dates or probabilities.
about2: Choose a path, then select a card or arrow to read more. Terms with dotted underlines open an explanation. Start the tour if you would like to explore the whole picture in order.
about3: “Observed examples,” “Evidence under limited conditions,” and “Conditional hypothesis” describe the kind of support available, not danger or completion percentages.
about4: A catastrophe, a loss of human agency, and human extinction are different outcomes. We separately ask whether people could survive a catastrophe and rebuild.
about5: Follow the connections from left to right. Horizontal position does not measure years. OR branches represent different mechanisms; AND frames group conditions considered together. Positions within a frame do not imply a time order either.
about6: Research acceleration and self-improvement appear by default within the control-loss and work-automation maps. You can fold them away on the map. They are treated as important factors, without making RSI or ASI a requirement.
about7: We distinguish publication dates, the periods studied, and the dates our explanations were reviewed. A lack of observed problems alone does not tell us whether safeguards are working.
about8: Sources link to original work by researchers and investigating organizations. The way conditions are grouped also includes editorial choices for this map. It does not prove that every pathway has exactly the necessary and sufficient conditions.
parallelGuide: Reading AND, OR, and parallel conditions
parallelHelp: OR branches show different mechanisms. AND frames group conditions needed together in this path. The card before a frame names the phenomenon those conditions explain. Lines crossing alone do not mean a junction.
fullMapHelp: “All elements” shows every registered item. Changes to work and money have destinations distinct from extinction. Dotted connections show influences on other paths. Select a card that is too small to read to zoom into it.
influenceHelp: Dotted connections show how one condition may enable or limit another. They are not mandatory steps. Select an arrow to read the conditions under which that influence might hold.
loadError: Details could not be loaded. Check your connection and try again.
storyNote: A conditional account, not a prediction of future events.
tourFocus: Select a step to zoom in
tourStartTitle: Where could we go from here?
tourStartText:
The work we can entrust to AI is changing. What happens next depends on its capabilities, how people use it, and the systems around it.

This tour explores seven possible paths from the present, along with research acceleration and self-improvement. Press Enter or the right arrow, or choose Next. You can also scroll the text. The diagram will follow.
tourOrderNote: The reading order is not necessarily the order of events. An AND frame groups conditions needed together; branches show different possibilities.
tourFinishTitle: Bring the next headline back to this map
tourFinishText:
The same advance in AI can matter for work and for control, but the conditions between that advance and each outcome differ. Research acceleration and self-improvement can affect several paths.

When you see a new headline, try placing it on the map: which condition has changed? That also helps reveal what we still don’t know.
optionalFactorHelp: Research acceleration and recursive self-improvement (RSI) are important factors for this path, but not mandatory steps. Folding the group away does not change the pathway’s meaning.
factorPickerHelp: A factor that can affect several paths, including control loss and work automation.
